memos.headline: S04 and S09 Lead on Relative Strength; S07 and S02 Breaking Down Below 50-Day Means
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. S04 stands out with a 4-week return of +26.6% and relative strength vs SPY of +23.0% over that period, sitting 15.1% above its 50-day mean — a powerful momentum thrust, though the extension raises near-term pullback risk. S09 is the cleanest uptrend: +10.8% above its 50-day, +15.8% above its 200-day, RSI 67.9, only -3.7% from its 52-week high, and positive relative strength across both 4w and 12w horizons. On the other side, S07 is the weakest name at -22.3% from its high, -8.6% below its 50-day mean, RSI 42.8, and bleeding relative strength at -11.0% vs SPY over 12 weeks — this is a broken chart until it reclaims ~900. S02 is similarly deteriorating with RSI 38.3, -5.7% below its 50-day, and 4-week relative strength of -10.9% vs SPY, suggesting sellers are in control near-term. I have moderate conviction on the leaders and the laggards; the middle of the pack (S10, S06, S01) is muddled and I'd stay neutral there.

views.note: Massive 4w momentum (+26.6%) with best-in-class relative strength vs SPY (+23.0% 4w, +15.1% 12w); would reassess if price breaks below 420 (~13% below current), which would negate the breakout.
Cleanest uptrend in the universe: near 52w highs (-3.7%), well above both moving averages, RSI 67.9, and positive relative strength on all timeframes; invalidation level is ~150 (below 200d mean).
Only -3.7% from 52w high and strong 12w relative strength (+15.4%), but 4w momentum has stalled (-0.5%) and RSI is middling at 48.5; needs to hold 340 to stay constructive.
Decent 4w bounce (+11.4%) but 12w return is still -4.9% and 12w relative strength is -6.9% vs SPY, suggesting this is a counter-trend rally rather than a new uptrend; watching 250 as support.
Worst drawdown in the universe at -22.3% from high, -8.6% below 50d mean, RSI 42.8, and 12w relative strength -11.0% vs SPY — clear downtrend; would reconsider above 900.
RSI 38.3 is the lowest in the group, -5.7% below 50d mean, 4w relative strength -10.9% vs SPY; sellers in control and I'd need a reclaim of 410 to turn neutral.

4w return of -7.1% and 4w relative strength of -10.7% vs SPY despite sitting near its 50d mean; trend is ambiguous but near-term momentum is clearly negative; would need a close above 320 to reconsider.
Trading below both 50d and 200d means, 26w return of -9.6% is the only negative in the universe on that timeframe, and persistent negative relative strength; broken intermediate trend.
Middling across the board — RSI 51, flat relative strength vs SPY, above both moving averages but 1w return of -4.6% suggests some near-term selling pressure; no edge either way.
12w return of -11.3% and 12w relative strength of -13.4% are concerning, but 4w bounce of +7.8% and improving short-term relative strength hint at a potential base; too early to commit.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 deliver extraordinary margin expansion; S09 and S01 show earnings compression that warrants caution
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between names with durable, expanding earnings power and those facing margin headwinds. S10 stands out with 85.2% YoY revenue growth, a 71.5% net margin, and net income up 210.6% on only $8.47B of total debt — the cleanest balance sheet and strongest operating leverage in the group. S05 is similarly remarkable: $119.80B in revenue at a 93.7% net margin with net income up nearly 298% YoY and minimal debt of $14.79B. On the other end, S09 posted just 2.4% revenue growth with net income down 45.8% and a razor-thin 4.9% margin, while S01 saw net income decline 15.8% on essentially flat revenue of $21.20B with $29.30B in debt — leverage that looks uncomfortable against shrinking earnings. I would need to see margin stabilization in S09 and S01 (specifically net margin recovering above 8% and 16%, respectively) before reconsidering those names.

views.note: 85% revenue growth, 71.5% net margin, 210% net income growth, and only $8.47B debt make this the highest-quality earnings profile in the universe.
93.7% net margin and ~298% YoY net income growth on $119.80B revenue with minimal leverage is extraordinary earnings power.
39.7% net margin, 17.7% revenue growth, 31.3% net income growth, and moderate $40.29B debt reflect durable, high-quality earnings.
$200.61B revenue growing 19.6% with net income up 244.9% is compelling, though $133B debt and 31.2% margin warrant monitoring leverage ratios.
24% revenue growth and 64.9% net income growth with 17.5% margin show improving fundamentals, but $36.21B debt on $20.54B revenue is elevated.
27.7% revenue growth and 36.9% margin are solid, but $460.52B in total debt is an outsized liability that could compress cash flow if rates stay elevated.
16.4% revenue growth and 27.2% margin are respectable but $82.30B debt and decelerating growth versus peers keep me on the sideline.
Revenue essentially flat at +0.4% YoY with a 4.9% net margin; the 61% net income bounce looks like a recovery off a depressed base rather than structural improvement.
Net income down 45.8% YoY to a 4.9% margin on barely growing revenue of $85.14B signals clear earnings deterioration.
Net income fell 15.8% on just 1.5% revenue growth with $29.30B debt against $21.20B revenue — leverage is uncomfortable with shrinking earnings.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause at 3.75% but Sticky 3.3% CPI and Rising Long Yields Argue Against Duration and Favor Banks Over Growth
memos.body: I see a clear pause regime: the Fed has held the upper bound at 3.75% for three months after cutting 75bp over the prior year, while headline CPI is running at 3.3% YoY—well above target and limiting further easing. The labor market is firm with unemployment at 4.10%, down 20bp over both three- and twelve-month horizons, which removes any urgency for additional cuts. The 10-year yield at 4.74% has climbed 41bp over the past year and the 10y-2y spread sits at +50bp, a modestly positive but flattening curve that supports bank net interest margins while punishing long-duration assets. My base case is an extended pause through year-end; a CPI print dropping below 3.0% or unemployment rising above 4.4% would shift me toward an easing call and a more constructive duration stance.

views.note: Banks benefit from a positive 10y-2y spread of 50bp and a stable fed funds rate supporting net interest margins.
Cyclicals are supported by a firm labor market (4.10% unemployment, declining) and no imminent recession signal from the yield curve.
Duration-sensitive growth faces headwinds from the 10y yield at 4.74%, up 41bp YoY, with no near-term easing catalyst.
Staples offer defensive positioning but lack a catalyst in a pause regime with solid employment; neither compelling nor risky.
Energy is macro-neutral here; the pause regime and firm economy are mildly supportive but rising long yields cap valuation upside.
Long-duration proxy likely pressured by the 17bp rise in 10y yields over just three months and sticky inflation keeping the Fed sidelined.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S03 and S04 Surge While S08 and S05 Slide on Results
memos.body: I am reading the earnings-season price reactions as the clearest sentiment signal across this universe. S03 (+15.3%) and S04 (+15.5%) posted outsized positive reactions to their late-July results, suggesting a genuine narrative shift to the upside that may still have legs three weeks later. Conversely, S08 (-7.4%) and S05 (-7.1%) saw sharp negative reactions on their results filings, and with no subsequent positive catalysts in the evidence, the negative tone likely persists. S07 delivered a solid +5.6% on its Aug 4 earnings, while S01 was mildly negative at -1.9% with a flurry of concurrent filings including a management change, which adds uncertainty. S09's July 1 filing flagged a delisting notice and material rights modification—a cluster of governance red flags that I treat as a durable negative sentiment overhang. I have highest conviction on the strong positive movers (S03, S04) and the governance-troubled S09; lower conviction on names where the reaction was modest or already digested.

views.note: A +15.3% earnings-day pop signals a major positive narrative shift that likely still has momentum.
The +15.5% post-results move is the largest positive reaction in the universe and suggests sentiment has decisively turned.
A +5.6% earnings reaction is constructive but more modest; sentiment is positive but not as compelling as S03/S04.
A -7.4% earnings-day drop with no subsequent positive catalyst leaves negative sentiment intact.
The -7.1% results reaction and a subsequent 'Other Events' filing with no visible positive catalyst keep tone negative.
Delisting notice, material rights modification, and governance overhaul in a single filing create a deeply negative sentiment overhang.
A mild -1.9% earnings reaction paired with a management change creates mixed signals; no clear directional sentiment.
A modest +2.5% earnings reaction and routine governance filings suggest stable but unremarkable sentiment.
Recent material agreement and new debt obligation (Aug 17) could shift tone either way; no earnings reaction to anchor a view.
A tepid +1.2% earnings reaction over a month ago has likely been fully absorbed; no fresh catalyst.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Plunging but Oil Spike Signals Residual Energy-Security Risk
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has collapsed 47.5% over three months to 222.5, and VIX has fallen to 16.01 (down 14% in a month), suggesting the market is pricing out near-term geopolitical tail risk from sanctions or trade-policy escalation. However, WTI crude at $89.75 is up 6.4% month-over-month even as it remains down ~12% over three months, which tells me a short-term supply disruption or energy-security concern is building that has not yet fully resolved. HY spreads at 2.75% are essentially flat, confirming credit markets see no imminent policy shock. Without specific GDELT conflict or sanctions headlines in the evidence, I treat the current environment as a structural de-escalation from earlier 2026 peaks, but the oil move keeps me cautious on names with concentrated energy-input or supply-chain exposure; a new round of export controls or sanctions re-escalation would change my view materially.

views.note: Three Reg FD filings in two weeks suggest active investor communication, but without policy-specific content I cannot take a directional view.
Falling policy uncertainty and stable credit spreads favor names with broad domestic exposure; 8-K Other Events filing on Aug 10 is benign absent adverse detail.
Two 8-K filings in July (Reg FD and Other Events) suggest corporate activity, but the oil price spike introduces input-cost uncertainty I cannot resolve without more detail.
Recent Reg FD disclosure and sharply declining policy uncertainty support a constructive stance; would flip to avoid if new export controls targeting its sector emerge.
July 8-K Other Events filing is too stale and generic to act on; geopolitical backdrop is improving but conviction is low.
Reg FD filing in early August is noted but without policy-relevant content; the rising oil price is a watch item for any energy-exposed operations.
